newsitem.title: UK: Redland up on buying, FTSE Index moves.
newsitem.headline: Redland up on buying, FTSE Index moves.

text.p: Shares in building materials group Redland Plc were firmer as the stock attracted some buying interest, market makers said on Thursday.
Dealers said there was nothing specific driving the shares, but hopes the group might be making progress with disposals could have helped. By 1210 GMT the stock was 11 pence higher at 345.5 pence.

Dealers said Redland had been tipped as a candidate to drop out of the FTSE 100 Index. The London Stock Exchange said the Index will be adjusted on Friday to accommodate British Gas's demerger this week.

Traders were uncertain whether Redland was likely to leave the Index. Some said the rise in the share price suggested it would remain, while others said the gain might not be sufficient to prevent it from dropping out.
The FTSE 100 Index comprises Britain's top 100 companies ranked by market capitalisation.
